definitions.explanation: The introductory section of a document, law, or constitution that explains its purpose and principles. Also used more generally for any introductory text placed before the main body.

examples.japanese: {憲法|けんぽう}の{前文|ぜんぶん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: To read the preamble of the constitution.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}の{前文|ぜんぶん}に{目的|もくてき}が{記|しる}されている。
examples.english: The purpose is stated in the preamble of the contract.

examples.japanese: {日本国|にほんこく}{憲法|けんぽう}の{前文|ぜんぶん}には、{平和主義|へいわしゅぎ}の{理念|りねん}が{掲|かか}げられている。
examples.english: The preamble of the Japanese constitution sets forth the principle of pacifism.

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the context of constitutions, laws, treaties, and formal contracts, where the preamble establishes the document's purpose, principles, and intent.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {憲法|けんぽう}の{前文|ぜんぶん}: preamble of a constitution
- {条約|じょうやく}の{前文|ぜんぶん}: preamble of a treaty
- {前文|ぜんぶん}に{述|の}べる: to state in the preamble

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {序文|じょぶん}: preface, foreword — used for books and literary works; written by the author or a third party
- {序論|じょろん}: introduction — the opening section of an academic paper or essay
- {全文|ぜんぶん}: full text — a homophone with a completely different meaning; uses {全|ぜん} (whole) instead of {前|ぜん} (before)

USAGE:
Be careful not to confuse {前文|ぜんぶん} (preamble) with the homophone {全文|ぜんぶん} (full text). Context usually makes the distinction clear.
